description: Dangerous-pattern rules for compiled languages: Go, Java/Kotlin, C#, C/C++.

rules.title: Command executed through a shell
rules.remediation: Invoke the binary directly with separate arguments - exec.Command("git", "clone", url) - so no shell parses metacharacters.

rules.title: SQL query assembled with Sprintf or concatenation
rules.remediation: Use placeholders: db.Query("SELECT * FROM t WHERE id = $1", id). database/sql parameterises for you.

rules.title: TLS certificate verification disabled
rules.remediation: Add the internal CA to the RootCAs pool instead of skipping verification.

rules.title: math/rand used for a security value
rules.remediation: math/rand is deterministic. Use crypto/rand for anything security-relevant.

rules.title: Weak hash algorithm
rules.remediation: Use sha256 for integrity. For passwords use golang.org/x/crypto/argon2 or bcrypt.

rules.title: Broken cipher (DES or RC4)
rules.remediation: Use AES-GCM or ChaCha20-Poly1305.

rules.title: template.HTML bypasses output escaping
rules.remediation: These types tell html/template the content is already safe. Only use them on values you constructed, never on input.

rules.title: HTTP server without read/write timeouts
rules.remediation: http.ListenAndServe has no timeouts, so a slow client can hold connections open indefinitely. Build an http.Server with ReadHeaderTimeout, ReadTimeout, and WriteTimeout set.

rules.title: Runtime.exec() with a built string
rules.remediation: Use ProcessBuilder with a List<String> of arguments and no shell.

rules.title: SQL statement built by concatenation
rules.remediation: Use PreparedStatement with bound parameters.

rules.title: Java native deserialization
rules.remediation: Native deserialization of untrusted bytes is remote code execution with a well-known gadget-chain toolkit. Use JSON with an explicit schema, or a serialization filter (ObjectInputFilter).

rules.title: Weak message digest
rules.remediation: Use SHA-256 or better. For passwords use PBKDF2, bcrypt, or Argon2.

rules.title: Cipher in ECB mode or a broken algorithm
rules.remediation: ECB leaks plaintext structure - identical blocks encrypt identically. Use AES/GCM/NoPadding with a unique IV per message.

rules.title: TrustManager or HostnameVerifier accepts everything
rules.remediation: An empty checkServerTrusted accepts any certificate, which defeats TLS entirely. Trust a specific CA or pin the certificate.

rules.title: java.util.Random used for a security value
rules.remediation: Use SecureRandom.

rules.title: XML parser created without disabling external entities
rules.remediation: Set FEATURE_SECURE_PROCESSING and disable doctype declarations: factory.setFeature("http://apache.org/xml/features/disallow-doctype-decl", true). Reported at low confidence because the hardening may appear on a later line - verify before acting.

rules.title: Spring expression parsed from a variable
rules.remediation: SpEL evaluation of user input is remote code execution. Use a fixed expression, or a SimpleEvaluationContext with no type access.

rules.title: Spring @CrossOrigin with a wildcard origin
rules.remediation: List the specific origins you intend to allow.

rules.title: Spring Security CSRF protection disabled
rules.remediation: Only safe for a stateless API that never authenticates via cookies. If sessions are cookie-based, this is exploitable.

rules.title: SQL command built by concatenation
rules.remediation: Use SqlParameter bindings, or Entity Framework's parameterised LINQ.

rules.title: Insecure .NET deserializer
rules.remediation: BinaryFormatter is unfixable and removed in .NET 9. Use System.Text.Json with a known type. TypeNameHandling other than None allows arbitrary type instantiation.

rules.title: Certificate validation callback always returns true
rules.remediation: Returning true accepts every certificate, including an attacker's. Validate properly or pin the expected thumbprint.

rules.title: Unbounded string function
rules.remediation: Use the bounded variants (strncpy/strlcpy, snprintf, fgets) and always check the destination size. gets() cannot be used safely at all.

rules.title: system() or popen() with a built command
rules.remediation: Use the exec family with an explicit argument vector.

rules.title: Non-literal format string
rules.remediation: Always pass a literal format: printf("%s", buf). An attacker-controlled format string can read and write memory.
